title: Research Journal #36 — When the Physics Pushes Back: New Investigations in WC and WD
html:
Returning to the Physics

On November 13 we investigated two ways a promising spacetime calculation can depend on parts of the physical system that are easy to overlook. In the wormhole communication track (WC), we asked what gravitational effects a bent relativistic beam could produce once the mechanism bending it was included. In the advanced propulsion track (WD), we compared subluminal warp-shell constructions and asked how their stress-energy changes with the metric assembly and the treatment of the exterior.

1. WC — Completing the Physical Source

WC-PO-1.7D VG4-B extended our straight-line beam work to a small bend. An electromagnetic bend transfers momentum between the beam, the field, and the matter that generates and supports the field. The linearized flat-background analysis expands the total stress-energy as:

T = T₍₀₎ + θT₍₁₎ + O(θ²)

Here, θ is the small bend angle. The completed first-order coefficient must satisfy:

∂μ T(1)μν = 0

Any flux through the chosen system boundary must be accounted for. [VG4-B checkpoint, §§7–8]

VG4-B4-N1 preserved an analytic negative result. Equal-and-opposite forces on separated point bodies balance the integrated momentum exchange. Each body still contributes a local divergence at its own location. The complete source must include the interaction that carries momentum and its associated stresses. [VG4-B checkpoint through B5, §6]

VG4-B4-C1 narrowed an earlier estimate. VG4-B3 gave the subsystem scaling:

δh₀ᵢ⁽ᴬ⁾ ∼ 4GΔP / (c³Rₐ)

Here, G is Newton’s gravitational constant, ΔP the magnitude of subsystem momentum transfer, c the speed of light, and Rₐ the subsystem-to-observer range. The quotient is dimensionless in SI units.

For the complete isolated system, the gravitational perturbation depends on the redistribution of energy, momentum, and stress throughout the source. The estimate provides no full-system amplitude or detector contamination bound. [VG4-B checkpoint, §§5–6, 9]

VG4-B6 earned a bounded analytic PASS. For a localized symmetric first-order stress-energy tensor with vanishing surface terms, the first-order total energy E₁ and momentum P₁ⁱ are constant. For a finite region with nonzero boundary flux, the enclosed energy and momentum obey a balance law. The constancy result applies to the complete isolated system under the vanishing-surface-term assumption.

The first-order energy and momentum differences vanish for a reference matched in those totals. With x⁰ = ct, the mass dipole is:

D₁ⁱ = c⁻² ∫ xⁱ T₍₁₎⁰⁰ d³x

It obeys:

dD₁ⁱ/dt = P₁ⁱ

d²D₁ⁱ/dt² = 0

Total angular momentum is conserved under the same isolation and symmetry assumptions. These results exclude a time-varying total-energy monopole and an accelerating total mass dipole driven by the internal bend.

Quadrupolar and near-zone structure can still occur at first order. Their magnitude and projection into a detector observable are undetermined. Even when the beam is locally straight, an upstream bend can influence the detector by the time of closest approach. In the flat-background timing estimate, the bend disturbance arrives at closest approach for an upstream distance of about βγb, where β is beam speed in units of c, γ is the Lorentz factor, and b is the detector's transverse offset. This scale concerns arrival timing. The amplitude requires the complete retarded source and detector response. [VG4-B checkpoint, §4] [VG4-B checkpoint, §8]

Physical-source disposition — HOLD. The next proposed step, VG4-B7, asks which first-order terms survive bend reversal and can couple to a detector at a specified position. The explicit localized conserved source, its near-zone curvature, the detector transfer function, and the apparatus contamination bound remain open. VG4-B produced Category 6 analytic evidence. [VG4-B checkpoint, §§11–12]

2. WD — Testing the Geometry, Source, and Boundary

We compared the published Fuchs et al. subluminal shell, the pinned public WarpFactory example, and the configurations associated with Le’s earlier preprint analyses and public warpax code.

A numerical result transfers between those configurations only to the extent that the relevant geometry, inputs, and evaluation methods agree.

WD-9C.1 — The public WarpFactory baseline

The v0.1 calculation, preserved as baseline v1.0, reconstructed the public WarpFactory example and used centered Cartesian differences on axial and transverse rays.

At the finest Cartesian step, h = 0.01 m, each of the three warped radial grids gave 258 PASS and 44 INCONCLUSIVE out of 302 sampled locations, with zero resolved Type IV outcomes.

PASS required all four pointwise energy-condition slacks to exceed an empirical 10⁻⁹ m⁻² screen. Two raw complex-pair candidates on different coarser radial grids were below the numerical floor and disappeared on the finest radial grid.

At about 23.9 m the pinned example has a regular static, spherically symmetric exterior with a real stress spectrum. The pointwise counts apply to the sampled rays and resolutions. [WD-9C.1]

WD-9C.2 — Reconciling configurations

Both currently served versions of Le’s On the boundary cost of source-consistent warp shells (v1, May 25, and v2, June 20) compare Gaussian and boxcar smoothing in §4.

The archived author data record zero NEC, WEC, or DEC violations among 13 interior probes and 22 Type IV classifications among 25 exterior probes for each kernel.

At the common worst capped probe, r = 23.87755102040816 m, the Gaussian and moving-average values of the smaller WEC/DEC diagnostic were about −0.00790458 and −0.00819218 in geometric stress units (m⁻²).

These values measure severity over a rapidity-capped observer search. The Type IV classification comes from the algebraic spectrum, and v2 explicitly distinguishes the capped diagnostic from that classification and from cap-free Type I slacks.

Version 3, Relativistic elastic shells: material support and cavity geometry (September 17), studies a different constitutive model and cavity effects. Its material prescription was outside the WD-9C.4 tests.

Sources: [Le v1 §4] · [Le v2 §4] · [Le v3] · [Archived author data]

The project’s 624 comparison rows document differences that matter even within one kernel family.

The Fuchs paper describes a hollow-shell pressure solve and a smoothing-span ratio of about 1.72. The pinned MATLAB example seeds pressure with a filled-sphere expression masked to the shell and uses about 1.79.

The inspected warpax configuration also differs in metric assembly, mass normalization, shift support, and outer radial handling.

The BTLB reconstruction resolved Type IV at the archived axial probe for both warpax profiles. The public WarpFactory reconstruction had a real spectrum there. The full author census and capped severity were outside the verified replay. [WD-9C.2]

WD-9C.3 — Isolating the translation

In the inspected assembly, the radial arguments and radial directions move with X = x − vt while the exterior shift is set to zero. Here t = ctSI has units of length and v = 0.02 is speed in units of c.

A complete coordinate pullback also changes the time–space and time–time metric components, using:

dX = dx − v dt

The mixed stress tensor at the corresponding event then changes by a similarity transformation, preserving its spectrum. The full pullback of the exact Schwarzschild control preserves vacuum.

The uncompensated assembly produced a resolved Type IV pair at the archived axial probe for both kernels and even with exact Schwarzschild radial inputs.

The complex pair and a negative null contraction establish a pointwise null energy condition violation there. This control shows that the explicit compact shift, pressure prescription, and smoothing are unnecessary for the pair at that probe.

The 442 saved records leave the onset and spatial extent open. [WD-9C.3]

WD-9C.4 — Testing the exterior and its junctions

The investigation separated smooth-region conservation, junction matching, and the behavior at infinity.

The contracted Bianchi identity guarantees conservation of the effective Einstein source in smooth regions, with six separate numerical divergence checks in the saved record. This identity supplies no constitutive dynamics.

The 19 m shift cutoff passes the layer-free test under the stated smooth-input assumptions. The ideal shared-node Hermite knots also pass the layer-free test, with finite curvature jumps permitted.

The tested 30 m outer clamp requires an Israel surface layer and leaves a spatial solid-angle defect and an r⁻² bulk-density tail. The radial volume factor makes the integrated tail diverge.

The smooth uncompensated Schwarzschild continuation is asymptotically flat with finite ADM energy and absolutely integrable Eulerian energy density. It requires nonvacuum stress, and the integral of the absolute Eulerian flux diverges logarithmically.

Sources: [Israel] · [WD-9C.4]

At the resolved Type IV points, the tested translated exterior requires nonvacuum stress that a perfect fluid cannot supply. At each such point, the tensor violates the null, weak, dominant, and strong energy conditions. The location of the continuum onset and the full spatial extent remain open.

An independently specified material source with regular evolution and matching remains open.

The record retains 471 evaluations, including 30 failed literal polynomial extrapolations (18 InvalidOperation and 12 LinAlgError), plus 36 separate junction records and six divergence checks.

The failures document numerical limitations of the extrapolation. [Maeda and Martínez] · [WD-9C.4]

Historical parity — HOLD (Path A inconclusive). The exact 2024 Fuchs figure inputs, Le’s historical executable and run environment, and exact interpax parity are still unresolved.

The findings apply to the frozen configurations and controls. The WD work contributes Category 6 analytic and Category 7 numerical results, including the negative and inconclusive outcomes. The reconstructed probe agreement is a bounded computational comparison. Historical verification of the full author census and the exact figure-generating spacetime remains open.

Adoption of a new WD model would require its own evidentiary basis.

3. What the Two Tracks Share

WC showed why a locally conserved description must include whatever exchanges momentum with the beam.

WD showed why a change in metric assembly can alter the required stress-energy and why smooth-region consistency leaves junctions and global sourcing to be tested.

The results constrain the specific sources and geometries we investigated.

The WD Cross-Stream Review v1.0, preserved November 13 Chicago time, synthesized the WD work through WD-9C.5 and recorded an informational handoff to BTLB-SIM.

It identified a bounded question about whether an external general-relativity provider can carry the three frozen controls with their coordinate conventions, stress projections, and provenance intact.

The handoff is a Category 5 engineering review and grants no implementation authority or scientific validation. The WC checkpoint preserves its own research handoff.

Sources: [WD Cross-Stream Review v1.0] · [VG4-B checkpoint]

4. What Comes Next

For WC, the proposed B7 symmetry analysis can narrow which first-order source terms warrant a complete curvature and detector calculation.

For WD, a historical comparison remains on hold pending recovery of the original figure inputs or execution records needed for a matched comparison.

Any further source investigation must account for the required stresses and matching conditions of the particular geometry under study.

This entry records analytic and computational research. It contains no Category 8 independent reproduction of the BTLB results or Category 9 physical experiments.

Faster-than-light communication, wormhole traversal, and warp propulsion remain undemonstrated here.

Literature Used in the WD Investigation

Jared Fuchs, Christopher Helmerich, Alexey Bobrick, Luke Sellers, Brandon Melcher, and Gianni Martire (2024). “Constant velocity physical warp drive solution.” Classical and Quantum Gravity 41(9), 095013. Primary published construction compared in WD-9C.1–9C.4. Use the versioned preprint for the equations and appendices referenced by the project. Journal DOI · arXiv:2405.02709v1.

  2. An T. Le (2026). “On the boundary cost of source-consistent warp shells.” arXiv:2605.25417v1 (May 25) and v2 (June 20), §4 in each. Historical comparison targets. Both currently served versioned texts include Gaussian and boxcar results. Version 2 explicitly distinguishes rapidity-capped severity from algebraic classification and discusses cap-free Type I slacks. v1 §4 · v2 §4.

  3. Hideki Maeda and Cristián Martínez (2020). “Energy conditions in arbitrary dimensions.” Progress of Theoretical and Experimental Physics 2020(4), 043E02. Direct mathematical reference for the pointwise Type IV energy-condition implications in WD-9C.4. Publisher record.

  4. W. Israel (1966). “Singular hypersurfaces and thin shells in general relativity.” Il Nuovo Cimento B 44, 1–14. Direct method reference for the outer-clamp surface stress in WD-9C.4. Original article · 1967 erratum.

Literature Consulted for Comparison or Broader Context

  1. An T. Le (2026). “Relativistic elastic shells: material support and cavity geometry.” arXiv:2605.25417v3 (September 17). WD-9C.4 discusses this revision as context. Its elastic-shell material prescription was outside the tested configuration. The earlier Fuchs verification section belongs to v1/v2. v3.

  2. Jessica Santiago, Sebastian Schuster, and Matt Visser (2022). “Generic warp drives violate the null energy condition.” Physical Review D 105, 064038. Comparative reference in WD-9C.4. The unit-lapse argument was outside the established metric hypotheses for the tested exterior. APS record.

Computational Sources

  1. WarpFactory, publicly preserved warp-shell example at commit 2f9240b7ac6c4798aefad87df9de719f3706d487 (May 6, 2024). Direct input to the WD-9C.1 public-example reconstruction and later configuration comparisons. Constructor · MATLAB live example · Interpolation helper.

  2. warpax, v1.0.0 (29b72124ea282386d15ec92f9c9ee332358446b5) and v1.1.1 (03584967318035c504858f513988a1fba5053b90). Direct code/data references for configuration and exterior tests. The archived v1.0.0 output supports the quoted per-kernel tallies. The v1.1.1 constructor and ADM assembly identify the inspected implementation. The exact runtime-to-publication mapping remains open. v1.0.0 author data · v1.1.1 constructor · ADM assembly.

Beyond the Light Barrier Records

  1. Beyond the Light Barrier Research Method, v1.2. Project methodology and evidence classification. The project mirror supplies the versioned document. A public canonical locator was not established.

  2. WC-PO-1.7D — VG4-B source-completion checkpoint, November 13, 2026. Project analytic record for B1–B6, including B4-N1 and B4-C1. Through B5 · Through B6.

  3. WD-9C.1 numerical baseline, November 13, 2026. Calculation v0.1, preservation v1.0. Pinned baseline.

  4. WD-9C.2 v1.0 — Configuration Reconciliation, November 13, 2026. Pinned record.

  5. WD-9C.3 v1.0 — Translation-Isolation and Physical Consistency, November 13, 2026. Pinned record.

  6. WD-9C.4 v1.0 — Exterior Source and Boundary Consistency, November 13, 2026. Pinned record.

  7. WD Cross-Stream Review v1.0, preserved November 13, 2026 Chicago time. Subsequent WD synthesis and BTLB-SIM handoff through WD-9C.5. GitHub release.

The BTLB GitHub locators require repository access. The WD technical papers establish the published constructions, comparison targets, and mathematical methods cited here. The BTLB primary records document the project's own analytic and numerical findings.
